flags.why: Giong means a detached bamboo branch, not a bamboo pole ([dictionary](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Giong)).
flags.fix: bamboo branch; example: Người ta lấy cành giong làm bờ giậu. = People use bamboo branches to make fences.

flags.why: The verb for sounding a drum or gong is gióng, which is a different word ([dictionary](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Gi%C3%B3ng)).
flags.fix: Remove this sense from giong and place it under gióng; example: Dân làng gióng trống mở hội.

flags.why: Gơ means to propagate sweet-potato vines or vegetables, not to train yam vines onto supports ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/g%C6%A1)).
flags.fix: to propagate sweet-potato vines or vegetables; example: Bà gơ dây khoai lang để lấy giống. = Grandma propagated sweet-potato vines for planting.

flags.why: This naval rank belonged to the former Republic of Vietnam navy and is not the current Vietnamese name for rear admiral ([rank explanation](https://www.sggp.org.vn/do-doc-pho-do-doc-chuan-do-doc-de-doc-tuong-duong-voi-cac-chuc-danh-nao-trong-quan-doi-nhan-dan-viet-nam-post122996.html)).
flags.fix: [historical] rear admiral in the former Republic of Vietnam navy

flags.why: The imperial military title is the meaning learners are most likely to encounter today.
Nghiêm trị is formal language for severe punishment and should not be presented as neutral casual wording.
Ưu phiền is literary wording for sorrow and worry, so the untagged noun encourages inappropriate casual use.
